0.long_answer: Individuals with X-linked Say–Meyer syndrome exhibit developmental delay and short stature, and brain imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) often reveals abnormalities in white matter. One notable finding is that the corpus callosum, the large bundle of nerve fibers that connects the two cerebral hemispheres, is abnormally thin in affected individuals. This abnormality in the corpus callosum may contribute to the neurological features observed in the syndrome.
